title: Algebra
note: Transcribed from the MTH2010 lecture notes into Aether; references follow the notes' numbering.

entries.title: In (ℤ, +) the inverse of n is −n
entries.source:
Let n : Int
Step: n + (-n) = 0
Step: n + 0 = n

entries.title: Addition in ℤₙ is well defined
entries.source:
Let i, j, k, l, n : Int
Assume hk: i = k (mod n)
Assume hl: j = l (mod n)
Therefore i + j = k + l (mod n)

entries.title: |Sₙ| = n! and counting k-cycles
entries.source:
Step: factorial(3) = 6
Step: 4! = 24
Let n : Nat
Assume n >= 1
Step: n! = n * (n - 1)!
Step: (4 * 3 * 2) / 3 = 8

entries.title: D₄ relations as exponent arithmetic
entries.source: Step: 2 + 2 = 0 (mod 2)

entries.title: (a⁻¹)⁻¹ = a
entries.source:
Theorem: "Inverse of an inverse"
Proof:
    Assume Group(G, op, e, inv)
    Given a : G
    Step: op(inv(a), a) = e
    Therefore inv(inv(a)) = a
QED

entries.title: (ab)⁻¹ = b⁻¹a⁻¹
entries.source:
Theorem: "Shoes and socks"
Proof:
    Assume Group(G, op, e, inv)
    Given a, b : G
    Step: op(op(a, b), op(inv(b), inv(a))) = e
    Therefore inv(op(a, b)) = op(inv(b), inv(a))
QED

entries.title: Cancellation
entries.source:
Theorem: "Left cancellation"
Proof:
    Assume Group(G, op, e, inv)
    Given a, u, v : G
    Assume h: op(a, u) = op(a, v)
    Step: u = op(inv(a), op(a, u))
    Step: = op(inv(a), op(a, v))
    Step: = v
QED

entries.title: The identity is unique
entries.source:
Theorem: "Uniqueness of the identity"
Proof:
    Assume Group(G, op, e, inv)
    Given f : G
    Assume hf: forall x : G, op(x, f) = x
    Step: op(e, f) = e
    Step: op(e, f) = f
    Therefore f = e
QED

entries.title: (ab)⁻¹ = b⁻¹a⁻¹, in the notes' notation
entries.source:
Theorem: "Shoes and socks, multiplicatively"
Proof:
    Assume Group(G, op, e, inv)
    Given a, b : G
    Step: (a * b) * (b^-1 * a^-1) = e
    Therefore (a * b)^-1 = b^-1 * a^-1
QED

entries.title: a²a³ = a⁵ in a group
entries.source:
Assume Group(G, op, e, inv)
Given a : G
Step: a^2 * a^3 = a^5
Step: a * a^-1 = e
Step: (a^-1)^-1 = a

entries.title: Assuming a group is abelian
entries.source:
Assume Group(G, op, e, inv)
Given a, b : G
Step: op(a, b) = op(b, a)
entries.explanation: A group need not be commutative: ab and ba are different words, and Sₙ (n ≥ 3) has elements that do not commute.

entries.title: n′[k]ₙ = [0]ₙ
entries.source:
Let k, n, d, k1, n1 : Int
Assume hk: k = d * k1
Assume hn: n = d * n1
Step: n1 * k = d * n1 * k1
Step: = n * k1
Therefore n1 * k = 0 (mod n)

entries.title: f(k) = [k]ₙ is a homomorphism
entries.source:
Let r, s, n : Int
Step: r + s = r + s (mod n)
Step: r + n = r (mod n)

entries.title: φ(k) = mk is an injective homomorphism
entries.source:
Theorem: "phi(k) = mk"
Proof:
    Let m, k1, k2 : Int
    Step: m * (k1 + k2) = m * k1 + m * k2
    Assume hm: m != 0
    Assume h: m * k1 = m * k2
    Step: m * (k1 - k2) = 0
    Therefore k1 = k2
QED

entries.title: The parity map on D₂ₙ
entries.source:
Let i, k : Int
Assume hk: Odd(k)
Step: i + 1 = i + k (mod 2)

entries.title: The kernel is closed under products
entries.source:
Theorem: "Kernel closed under products"
Proof:
    Assume Group(G, op, e, inv)
    Assume Group(H, star, eH, invH)
    Assume hom: forall x : G, forall y : G, f(op(x, y)) = star(f(x), f(y))
    Given g1, g2 : G
    Assume k1: f(g1) = eH
    Assume k2: f(g2) = eH
    Step: f(op(g1, g2)) = star(f(g1), f(g2))
    Step: = star(eH, eH)
    Step: = eH
QED

entries.title: The kernel is closed under inverses
entries.source:
Theorem: "Kernel closed under inverses"
Proof:
    Assume Group(G, op, e, inv)
    Assume Group(H, star, eH, invH)
    Assume hom: forall x : G, forall y : G, f(op(x, y)) = star(f(x), f(y))
    Assume he: f(e) = eH
    Given g : G
    Assume k: f(g) = eH
    Step: eH = f(e)
    Step: = f(op(g, inv(g)))
    Step: = star(f(g), f(inv(g)))
    Step: = star(eH, f(inv(g)))
    Step: = f(inv(g))
QED

entries.title: R is reflexive
entries.source:
Assume Group(G, op, e, inv)
Assume Subgroup(H, G, op, e, inv)
Given x : G
Step: op(inv(x), x) = e
Therefore op(inv(x), x) in H

entries.title: R is symmetric
entries.source:
Theorem: "R is symmetric"
Proof:
    Assume Group(G, op, e, inv)
    Assume Subgroup(H, G, op, e, inv)
    Given x, y : G
    Assume h: op(inv(x), y) in H
    Step: inv(op(inv(x), y)) = op(inv(y), x)
    Therefore op(inv(y), x) in H
QED

entries.title: R is transitive
entries.source:
Theorem: "R is transitive"
Proof:
    Assume Group(G, op, e, inv)
    Assume Subgroup(H, G, op, e, inv)
    Given x, y, z : G
    Assume h1: op(inv(x), y) in H
    Assume h2: op(inv(y), z) in H
    Step: op(op(inv(x), y), op(inv(y), z)) = op(inv(x), z)
    Therefore op(inv(x), z) in H
QED

entries.title: Euclidean division: a R r in ℤ/nℤ
entries.source:
Let a, k, n, r : Int
Assume a = k * n + r
Step: a = r (mod n)
Step: -a + r = (-k) * n

entries.title: Subgroups of abelian groups are normal
entries.source:
Assume AbelianGroup(G, op, e, inv)
Given x, h : G
Step: op(op(x, h), inv(x)) = h

entries.title: Kernels are normal
entries.source:
Theorem: "Kernels are normal"
Proof:
    Assume Group(G, op, e, inv)
    Assume Group(K, star, eK, invK)
    Assume hom: forall x : G, forall y : G, f(op(x, y)) = star(f(x), f(y))
    Assume hinv: forall x : G, f(inv(x)) = invK(f(x))
    Given x, h : G
    Assume kh: f(h) = eK
    Step: f(op(op(x, h), inv(x))) = star(f(op(x, h)), f(inv(x)))
    Step: = star(star(f(x), f(h)), invK(f(x)))
    Step: = star(star(f(x), eK), invK(f(x)))
    Step: = eK
QED
